reviewers.summary: The primary completion-placement behavior is mostly consistent, and the Spec Kit artifact checker passes. Four agent-resolvable inconsistencies remain: an unsupported no-motion fallback, bundled dependency work outside the stated feature scope, contradictory ADR amendment mechanics, and owner-isolation behavior that is planned but not frozen as acceptance.

The revised plan now provides proportionate evidence for filtering, paging, account isolation, motion timing, failure, reduced motion, exact-SHA delivery, and production restoration. Three planning gaps remain: tasks are not organized into the required test-first US1 lanes, success-criterion traceability is not mechanically closed, and two new interaction-safety claims lack explicit tests. product_decisions.affected_acceptance: FR-001 ('partition loaded results into open tasks followed by a labelled Completed section'), SC-001 ('A completed task appears exactly once below all loaded open tasks'), SC-003 (filtered views still display completed tasks through existing include-completed behavior), and design.md states S13 (pagination) and S14 (filtered or grouped completion).
options: Unbounded as specified: every loaded completed task renders in the Completed section, accepting that open rows share the 50-row page budget with completed history and may require paging to reach.

Bound by recency: the Completed section shows only tasks completed within a recent window (for example today, or the last 7 days); older completed work stays reachable through the existing history path.

Bound by count: the Completed section shows the most recent N completed tasks (for example 20) with the remainder reachable through the existing history path, keeping the open list's page budget effectively intact.
product_decisions.question: How much completed history should the always-visible Completed section show by default in a task list?
product_decisions.why_needed: The spec freezes scope to animation and open/completed placement with no new filters (spec.md:54-55), and reuses `include_completed` unchanged. That combination mechanically yields an unbounded Completed section: `complete` never reassigns `order_key` (service.py:702-711), the sort key has no completed dimension (service.py:1583-1595), and the server truncates at 50 (service.py:843, tasks.py:970). For a long-lived account the first page becomes mostly completed history and the open work the feature exists to surface is pushed behind repeated 'Load more'. The implementing agent cannot bound the section on its own, because any bound adds default behavior the owner explicitly excluded from scope — so the choice needs the owner.

reviewers.summary: The core completion behavior is coherent, but the artifacts leave two binding contract conflicts unresolved and omit acceptance treatment for counts and filtered/reloaded views. The owner's product direction is already explicit, so no further product decision is required.

The feature is buildable in the named files (TaskListPage.tsx, its Vitest suite and frontend/tests all exist, and the include-completed query support the plan relies on is real), but the plan's central architectural assertion — that no server-side change is needed because "loaded pages are flattened then partitioned" — does not survive contact with the code. `complete` leaves `order_key` untouched, `_sort_key` has no open/completed dimension, and the server truncates at `all_filtered[:limit]` (default 50), so always-on `include_completed` makes completed history compete with open tasks for the page window and can push the owner's open work off the loaded list entirely. The plan also mis-describes the control it intends to change ("existing cancelled-history toggle" — there is no such control; there is one "Show completed" checkbox driving both flags), which conceals that the change deletes the only way to hide completed work; that rename silently breaks two Playwright specs and one Vitest assertion the plan says it preserves. Rollback is under-stated because the candidate bundles an unrelated Tailwind/TypeScript/ESLint downgrade whose revert re-breaks the frontend build. One genuine product fork remains: the spec freezes scope to "no new filters", which mechanically yields an unbounded Completed section, and the implementing agent cannot bound it without contradicting that freeze — so the owner must choose. Layering, data ownership and ADR-0008 landing class are clean: the change is frontend-presentation only, touches no repository/service boundary, and every path it modifies classifies SHIP.

The chosen evidence layers are appropriate, but the package does not yet map every acceptance outcome to concrete assertions. Filter/reload and cancelled-history behavior are under-specified, motion evidence lacks measurable trigger/timing checks, existing required Playwright tests encode the superseded behavior, dependency repair is sequenced after tests that require it, and production cleanup is not executable through the current Task controls. These are implementation-planning issues; no product decision is required. No tests were run and no files were changed.

Four rubric areas pass on the artifacts plus code verification, and three do not. Passing: no new path sends user content to a remote provider, so the consent questions are genuinely N/A (spec.md:61-63, plan.md:9 — verified: the change only flips an existing query parameter, and the flag-gated title-completion path at backend/app/api/tasks.py:136-208 logs only ids/provider/duration). Owner scoping holds server-side — GET /api/tasks resolves through task_repo.list_for_owner(owner_id=...) (backend/app/modules/tasks/service.py:823) and no new endpoint is added, so the 404-vs-403 question does not arise. No new durable record type is created (spec.md:40), and tasks in every state are already covered by account purge and by the ZIP export (docs/data-retention.md:16,131-133), so there is no deletion or export gap. No invite code, session token or correlation ID becomes an authorization input; completion stays idempotent and is never shown before the canonical acknowledgement (design.md:45); no new credential or provider config appears. Failing: (1) plan.md:31 and SC-004 make production screenshots of the task list a delivery deliverable on precisely the surface this feature fills with real task titles by default — Constitution Principle I (.specify/memory/constitution.md:41) forbids real user data in PR evidence, and the artifacts name no synthetic identity, no crop/redaction rule and no closed field list; (2) plan.md:17 writes the completed row into a process-global query cache that deliberately survives sign-out and account switch and is keyed without an account id, so the widened default payload (now including completed history) can paint for the wrong owner; (3) plan.md:31's "clean up synthetic work through existing controls" names a control that does not fully exist — there is no task delete/erase endpoint, and a synthetic task left completed is now permanently visible by default. Separately, the bundled "build repair" is a partial rollback of a merged Dependabot group update with no advisory check recorded. All four are settleable by the implementing agent; no product decision is required — the owner has already decided default completed visibility (spec.md:53-57) and the mobile/web scope split (spec.md:61).

Feature 016 is a frontend-presentation-only change (default-visible Completed section, canonical-success-triggered movement, grey-strikethrough styling) over the existing TaskListPage. The spec/plan/design package is unusually thorough for this rubric: 15 named states across D-01/M-01 cover loading, both empty variants, fetch error with correlation-ID mention, save failure/interruption, partial (mixed-outcome) completion, completed-only, pagination, filtered/grouped completion, and reduced-motion/keyboard — all bidirectionally mapped to FR-001..FR-003 with no orphaned affordances or requirements. Keyboard/focus handling (focus transfers to the title link when the completion button disappears) matches the real, tested code pattern at frontend/src/features/tasks/TaskListPage.tsx:842 and frontend/src/features/tasks/__tests__/TaskListPage.test.tsx:1469. Mobile viability targets the rubric's exact 390x851 viewport, preserves 44px targets, and explicitly states primary-loop impact per Principle V. No forbidden ADR-0006 terminology, no new destructive action, and no color-only status signaling (checkmark + strikethrough + heading, not grey alone). The claimed supersession of spec 011 FR-029 and the referenced design-skill validator script were both verified against the repository. No blocking or important findings surfaced; the three findings below are advisory polish/clarity items only, so the lens returns pass.

technical_findings.description: The plan's load-bearing claim that always-on `include_completed` needs no server change is false: completed tasks keep their open-state `order_key`, the sort key has no open/completed dimension, and the server truncates the result at `limit` (default 50) before the client ever partitions it — so completed history competes with open tasks for the page window and can push open work off the loaded list.

technical_findings.recommendation: State in plan.md how the open list stays complete once completed rows share the page budget. Either fetch the Completed section as its own bounded query (a second `useTaskList` with `state`-less `include_completed` and a small `limit`) so the open query keeps its full 50 slots, or make the ordering completed-aware server-side. If the 'no server change' constraint is kept, plan.md must say explicitly that page composition now mixes open and completed rows, that reaching all open work may require repeated 'Load more tasks', and that the agent-run-summaries 200-id cap is reached sooner.

The plan describes a single FLIP pass while the code fires an independent autosave controller plus a list invalidation per completed row, so overlapping completions produce interleaved refetch and layout passes with no stated behavior.
evidence: specs/016-completed-task-animation/plan.md:3 — 'Design: `design.md` and the owner's annotated screenshots' — no D-01/M-01 or S01–S15 id appears anywhere in plan.md.

specs/016-completed-task-animation/plan.md:17 — 'Capture old row rectangles before applying a completed task, then use a layout effect and Web Animations API to move existing matching task rows from their old to new positions' — written for one row transition, with nothing about a second completion arriving mid-flight.

frontend/src/features/tasks/TaskListPage.tsx:444-454 — `onComplete` builds a fresh `getTaskDetailAutosaveController` per row whose acknowledgement calls `invalidateTasks()` (line 448); two rapid completions therefore queue two independent refetches of every loaded page.
frontend/src/features/tasks/TaskListPage.tsx:192,208 — `invalidateTasks` / `applyCanonicalTask` re-render the list asynchronously, which can reorder rows while a FLIP animation is still running.
technical_findings.recommendation: Name the design states the plan realizes (at minimum S02, S03, S10, S11, S13, S15) and add one paragraph on overlapping completions: whether a second completion cancels, queues behind, or runs concurrently with an in-flight animation, and what the FLIP pass does when the invalidation refetch re-renders the list mid-animation. Prefer reusing the existing `applyCanonicalTask` (TaskListPage.tsx:193-209) so the list cache patch is synchronous and the animation is not gated on a network round trip.

technical_findings.description: On every view where no GTD state is selected — project, tag, and the overdue/today/upcoming date views, plus the default list — the header count is computed from the raw fetched array, so always-including completed tasks silently changes it from an open-task count to an open-plus-completed-loaded-so-far count that grows with each 'Load more'. design.md states the heading and subtitle are unchanged.

technical_findings.description: SC-003 and the cancelled-history separation do not have explicit evidence assignments. This is a changed seam: the current implementation and test intentionally couple both terminal-state flags.

Update one real-stack Playwright journey to retain the completed task through a representative filtered reload. Reuse existing backend tests rather than adding backend behavior tests.

technical_findings.description: The browser evidence is described only as verifying “actual movement.” It does not define assertions for the 600ms ceiling, the post-canonical-response trigger, or the prohibition on animation during initial load and filter navigation. Consequently SC-002 can pass even if movement is late or begins optimistically, and the explicitly excluded animation triggers can regress unnoticed.

specs/016-completed-task-animation/checklists/requirements.md:5-6 claims bounded evidence although the timing and trigger boundary are not bounded by the stated test plan.

technical_findings.description: The task order is internally unexecutable if the plan's broken-toolchain claim is current: T002 requires focused failing tests before T003 performs the dependency repair needed to run tests. T003 also combines writer-owned package repair and validation with independent exact-candidate review/QA, obscuring the immutable candidate boundary. technical_findings.description: The delivery plan makes production screenshots a required evidence artifact on the one surface whose entire purpose is rendering task titles, and this feature makes the account's completed history render there by default — with no artifact stating which account is used, whether it is synthetic, or what may appear in a recorded image. plan.md:31 instructs: 'Verify synthetic completion and reload in production at mobile/desktop widths, record screenshots/run links', and SC-004 (spec.md:49) elevates 'browser evidence' to an acceptance criterion. FR-001 (spec.md:34) requires the web view to request completed items by default and render them in a labelled Completed section, so a full-width production screenshot now necessarily carries the surrounding real open rows plus the account's real completed history — not just the one synthetic row. Constitution Principle I (.specify/memory/constitution.md:41) states that real user data MUST NOT enter logs, metrics, committed fixtures, or PR evidence; the repository already has a worked precedent for exactly this shape of evidence, docs/external-agent-relay-release.md:346-369, which closes the field list and states that 'the handed-off Task's title, its details, or its supporting items' may not appear 'in any form, including inside a screenshot ... If a screenshot would carry a single field from the second list, it is not evidence, it is a leak.' Neither spec.md, plan.md, design.md nor tasks.md (T004, tasks.md:6, which is where 'record acceptance/traceability/report' lands) carries any equivalent constraint.

technical_findings.description: The plan writes completed rows into a shared client cache whose task entries deliberately survive sign-out and an A→B account switch and are keyed without an account identifier, so the widened default payload can be painted for the wrong owner. plan.md:17 says 'Use canonical autosave acknowledgements to update the list/detail cache immediately', and FR-001 makes completed content part of every default list response (spec.md:34, plan.md:13 'Request includeCompleted=true'). That cache is the process-global QueryClient at frontend/src/queryClient.ts:8, whose only session bindings are bindRelaySession and bindAdminSession (:10-11). Sign-out clears the auth store only (frontend/src/stores/authStore.ts:107-117), and the retention of task entries across a session change is deliberate and asserted: frontend/src/__tests__/queryClient.test.ts:40-42 comments 'Admin-only purge: task/account/relay records survive a session change' and asserts a ['tasks','next'] entry still holds its data after clearSession(). taskKeys.list(filters) (frontend/src/api/taskHooks.ts:9) contains no account id, and after this change the default filter object is identical for every account (includeCompleted is no longer derived from the per-session showCompleted state at frontend/src/features/tasks/TaskListPage.tsx:83,134-135), so the next signed-in owner hits the previous owner's entry. This gap predates the feature, but the feature widens the retained payload from open tasks to open plus completed history while plan.md:9 asserts 'No consent/processor/retention or telemetry change' — the artifacts never mention cache lifetime or account-switch behaviour at all.

Option (b) contradicts the deliberate policy recorded at frontend/src/__tests__/queryClient.test.ts:40-41, so if it is chosen, update that test's assertion and comment in the same change rather than leaving two sources of truth. Add a Vitest case that seeds a completed-task list entry for account A, drives clearSession() then a sign-in as account B, and asserts B's first paint contains none of A's titles.

technical_findings.description: The production verification step creates a durable task record in a production account and promises cleanup 'through existing controls', but no control erases a task, and under this feature the residue is now visible by default. plan.md:31 requires observing 'synthetic completion and reload in production' and then to 'clean up synthetic work through existing controls'. There is no task delete or erase endpoint: backend/app/api/tasks.py exposes create, PATCH /tasks/{task_id} (:886) and POST /tasks/{task_id}/transitions (:908) only — the single @router.delete at :691 is for tags — and the service's terminal states are 'completed' and 'cancelled' (backend/app/modules/tasks/service.py:527,723; _OPEN_STATES at :57). Spec 011's Trash and explicit erasure (specs/011-rtm-task-parity/spec.md FR-012/FR-013/FR-037-039) are planned, not built. So a synthetic production task can only be cancelled, and persists in the production data store until account purge (docs/data-retention.md:16). Because FR-001 now makes completed items visible by default, a synthetic task left in 'completed' would remain permanently on screen in that account's list — cleanup therefore has to be an explicit cancel transition, which no artifact says.

Promote the cleanup from a trailing clause to a checked outcome in T004 (tasks.md:6).

technical_findings.description: The plan folds an unrelated dependency rollback into this SHOW-class landing and describes it in terms that understate what it does, with no record that the reverted versions are advisory-free. plan.md:27-29 calls it a 'necessary package/lock repair' that 'restores only demonstrated compatible constraints' and 'changes no source or gate configuration'. The working-tree diff of frontend/package.json is in fact a partial revert of the merged Dependabot group update (commit 33bd442, PR #191, 'bump the frontend-dependencies group across 1 directory with 26 updates'): typescript ^7.0.2→~6.0.3, eslint ^10.9.1→^9.39.5, eslint-plugin-react-hooks ^7.1.1→^5.2.0, tailwindcss ^4.3.3→^3.4.19, jsdom ^30.0.1→^24.1.3, allure ^3.16.0→~3.14.3, and the runtime dependency @tanstack/react-query ^5.102.8→~5.101.4. Two claims do not hold: downgrading TypeScript and ESLint across majors changes what the type and lint gates enforce, and @tanstack/react-query ships to production, so this is not tooling-only. .github/dependabot.yml:3-7 records that this watcher exists precisely because 'advisories accumulated silently', yet no artifact states that none of the reverted versions reintroduces a known advisory. Nothing mechanical will ask: scripts/classify_path_risk.py:58-88 classifies frontend/package.json as SHIP (no ASK prefix, exact path or risk token), and it is not in the GUARDED_FILES list at scripts/check_gate_integrity.py:41-61. ADR-0008 puts 'dependency patches' in SHIP (docs/decisions/0008-verified-trunk-serial-landing.md:56-58); a cross-major rollback of a security-motivated group update is not a dependency patch, and a security regression would fall under the ASK class at :62-64.

technical_findings.recommendation: Record in plan.md the advisory status of every reverted package at its pinned version — run `npm audit --omit=dev` plus a dev-scope `npm audit` against the repaired frontend tree and paste the counts — and state explicitly that no reverted version reintroduces a known advisory. Correct the two inaccurate claims in plan.md:29 (the revert does change what the tsc/eslint gates enforce, and @tanstack/react-query is a runtime dependency). Land the repair as its own candidate ahead of the UI change so its evidence is separable and rollback of one does not force rollback of the other. If any reverted version does carry an advisory, escalate that candidate to ASK per ADR-0008:62-74 instead of relying on the path classifier's SHIP verdict.

technical_findings.description: The zero-completed-tasks condition (Completed heading fully absent, as opposed to rendered empty) is only inferable from the phrase 'any matching completed tasks' in S01 and from the static HTML's 'before' frame; it isn't named as its own state the way first-run vs. filtered-empty (S06/S07) are explicitly distinguished.
evidence: specs/016-completed-task-animation/design.md:27 (S01 default) — 'Open tasks first; any matching completed tasks under one Completed heading; no entry animation'
specs/016-completed-task-animation/design/task-completion.html — the 'D-01 · Desktop · Before completion' frame renders no `.completed` section markup at all when the completed count is zero
technical_findings.recommendation: State explicitly that the Completed heading renders only when at least one completed task is loaded, so implementers don't render an empty 'Completed (0)' heading instead of omitting the section.
